title: Hari-kathā — Śrīla B.B. Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja
subtitle: Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha
description: Recorded Hari-kathā discourses — the transcendental narrations of Śrīla Bhakti Ballabh Tīrtha Gosvāmī Mahārāja and the Śrī Chaitanya Gauḍīya Maṭha.

articles.title: A Short Narration on Rathayatra
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: This audio clip is taken from Srila Gurudev’s harikatha held via video conference at Kolkata Math in 2004. He states that all the services offered to Lord Jagannath Dev at Puri temple are ordered by Jagannath Deva Himself and one of such services the Lord wanted to accept from His devotees is the cart festival. He narrates the mood of Sriman Mahaprabhu while taking Jagannath to Gundicha temple. He also explains the deep-rooted meaning of Rathayatra mentioned in Katha Upanishad.

blocks.text: Indradyumn Maharaj did not do anything by his own whims. You should very carefully note. Whatever he did, he did for the satisfaction of Baladeva, Subhadra and Jagannath. They appeared at the seashore in the form of wooden images, all transcendental wooden images, with all the marks of Supreme Lord. Indradyumn Maharaj was instructed, by Jagannath Deva, to perform Chandan Yatra, smearing of white sandal paste on the transcendental body of Baladeva, Suabhadra and Jagannath. It starts from the 'akshaya-tritiya' day, 'akshaya' means undecaying, whatever you do on that day will be undecaying. It is the third lunar day of the month of Vaishakh, which is the first calendar month according to the Bengali calendar. Chandan Yatra starts from that day and continues for twenty-one days. After that the king (Indradyumn Maharaj) wanted the service of Jagannath always, so Jagannath Deva said, “You perform the festival of bathing ceremony. I appeared on Jestha Poornima", the full-moon day of second calendar month, Jestha month. Jagannath said, "You are to bathe Me, with the water from the well which is at ‘akshaya-vat’ which contains water of all the holy rivers". 'Akshaya-vat' is undecaying banyan tree. This is bathing ceremony. After that again the king wanted another service. Then Lord Jagannath said, "You do Rathayatra". After the bathing ceremony, our Jagannath Deva made the pastimes of being ill, ill of fever. They do not offer food during those pastimes, they give some sort of liquid thing because He has fever and He cannot take regular food for fifteen days! And then beautification of His body, after fifteen days He appears, that is called 'nava-yauvanam-utsava', rejuvenated festival or 'netrotsava', His festival of the eyes, the organ of vision. He appears and orders to perform Rathayatra, "I want to see all the devotees, many of the devotees are not allowed to enter in the temple, I want to see them and they should be given the scope to see Me. If they will see Me they will get eternal welfare." So taking the permission of Lakshmi Devi He leaves. From Jagannath temple to Gundicha. Gundicha is Vrindavan according to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Jagannath Dham (temple) is Kurukshetra. Gopis, they took Krishna from Kurukshetra, they have served Krishna, they have connection with Krishna, but the paraphernalia is something not congenial, everything here is with majestic aspect which they do not like, He should go to the sweet Vrindavan, “He Gopinath! He Gopinath Vrindavane chalo he Gopinath!" By saying that pulling the Ratha, the chariot and taking Him to Vrindavan means Gundicha. Chaitanya Mahaprabhu did this. We belong to Chaitanya Mahaprabhu's school of thought. We should pull the chariot with that mood of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. Taking Krishna from the majestic aspect to the sweet realm, Vrindavan Dham. There is also evidence you will find in Rig veda, 'dārupravati sindhupāre apūrusam' etc. There is no time to explain in detail.
In Kaṭha Upanishad (1.3.3-4), the deep rooted meaning of Rathayatra is mentioned,

Ātma is the owner of the chariot, master of the chariot or the main hero in the chariot who fights. This body is the Ratha, the chariot. The charioteer (sārathi) is buddhi (the intellect), but not this material intellect. You will find,
Sri Krishna says in Bhagavad Gita, "One who has got devout devotion to Me, (the Supreme Lord, Sri Krishna) I give him the wisdom to understand how he can get Me".

That sort of intellect. Not this material intellect. This is the highest spiritual knowledge. That buddhi-yoga, you will find in Gita, teṣāṁ satata-yuktānāṁ bhajatāṁ prīti-pūrvakam, you worship Krishna with pure love, with devout devotion, then Lord will show you the path, will give you the intelligence and understanding on how to worship. The strings indicate the mind. And the horses are the sense organs, the impetus of sense organs are taking us to the non-eternal things of the world to attach us to the non-eternal things of the worlds. For that reason, those horses are controlled through the reins, controlled by the charioteer (sārathi) through the mind. And when you serve Supreme Lord, Sri Krishna with all the senses organs, and everything, then your life will be successful. This is deep-rooted significance, you will find in Kaṭha Upanishad.

articles.title: Glories of Gambhira and Siddha Bakul
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: In this harikatha, Srila Gurudev narrates the glories of Gambhira where Mahaprabhu performed the most intense pastimes of being fully absorbed in the divine mood of Srimati Radhika. He also narrates the glories of Siddha Bakul where Haridas Thakur, a personal associate of Mahaprabhu performed intense bhajan and from where he entered into nityalīlā. While narrating a few important pastimes, Srila Gurudev strongly emphasizes the teachings Mahaprabhu and Haridas Thakur gave us through their lives and how a sadhaka should spend his life with only one goal of satisfying the Supreme Lord Sri Krishna.

blocks.text: We came here at Haridas Thakur’s samādhi after having darśan of Gambhira and Radhakant Math. This area is under the garden of Gambhira, Kashi Mishra’s house; it is not outside of it. King Prataparudra’s father King Purushottam Deva went to fight and conquer South India and by defeating the King of Kanchi, he brought Radhakant and Sakshi Gopal here in Puri. He also brought Bhand Ganesh, a throne of jewels and many other things. He kept all that in the Jagannath temple. The Radhakant vigrah was kept near to the pādpith of Mahaprabhu. Though Kashi Mishra was the family guru of King Prataparudra, the King was serving him with a very strong faith like his spiritual master. The King used to serve him before starting his daily routine.

We have heard the name of Vasudeva Sarvabhaum, he was incarnation of Brihaspati himself. He appeared in Nabdwip Dham. He was not an ordinary person. He had all the knowledge but he was enacting the pastimes of a Māyavadi and he was engaged in preaching the thoughts of Māyavadis. When Mahaprabhu rescued him, he mentioned to the King Prataparudra that Mahaprabhu is not an ordinary person, He is Supreme Lord Krishna Himself. The King said, “You are very learned person, you have knowledge of all the scriptures if you are saying that He is Lord Himself then it must be true. So, please make some arrangement so that I also could get His darśan and make my life successful.” Sarvabhaum replied, “Mahaprabhu would come back from His South India tour in a few days after rescuing the conditioned souls there. Where would He stay? A secluded, peaceful place should be arranged for Him near the temple.” In response to which the King suggested the house of Kashi Mishra. Then, Sarvabhaum went to Kashi Mishra and informed him that the King is suggesting his house for Mahaprabhu's stay. Kashi Mishra became very pleased on hearing that and said that it would be his good fortune if Mahaprabhu would stay at his place. They made an arrangement for Mahaprabhu's stay. Kashi Mishra was worshipable for the King as he was like his guru, so when Kashi Mishra expressed his desire to serve Radhakant vigrah then the vigrah was shifted from temple to his house, the place where they are now and from then onwards it is called Radhakant Math. Inside Radhakant Math there is a small hut made up of clay, known as Gambhira where Mahaprabhu, the tall figured personality, stayed. Govinda used to serve His transcendental body there. Swarup Damodar and Ray Ramanand used to serve Mahaprabhu by intensifying His mood of relishing the highest Divine Love of Radharani.

One pastime took place that time from which we can learn something. If we become too attached to the rules and regulations then we will not have devotion. Following rules and regulations is good but not understanding their actual intentions, if we get too much attached to them then that will not help us in our devotion. Not following the rules will also harm our devotion. One pastime took place here. Every day after lunch prasādam, Govinda used to serve Mahaprabhu's lotus feet until Mahaprabhu would go to sleep. Everyday Mahaprabhu used to dance in ecstatic feelings and get tired. One day He was so tired and was sleeping in such a position that Govinda was not able to serve His feet in that position. Govinda requested Him to change His position so that he could serve Him. Mahaprabhu told him, “I am too tired, and will not move now”. So how could Govinda serve Him in that position? He thought, “It is my service and I have to do that.” Govinda took his upper cloth and covered Mahaprabhu’s transcendental body with it and crossed Him. Generally, in the scriptures it is written that crossing even the shadow of someone's body is an offense but here he crossed the body of the Lord, the Supreme, and went to the other side to serve Him. Mahaprabhu went into a deep sleep and when He woke up it was three o'clock in the afternoon. He saw Govinda and asked him, “What happened, did you not go for your lunch?”
He replied, “How can I go?”
“Just like you came, you can go the same way” Mahaprabhu replied.
Govinda told, “I crossed your transcendental body to serve You and now for serving my belly, how can I cross You?”
This is the teaching. He broke the rules to serve Mahaprabhu.

I am in the temple serving the deities and suddenly Guruji comes and calls out my name. At that time if I think that I cannot go without completing the deity worship and if, not seeing me around, Guruji goes back then that will be considered as an offense. I have to immediately come out and serve him first. First Guru-puja and then by his order Gauranga-puja and then the worship of RadhaKrishna. By being too much attached to the rules, if you ignore Guru then that would be considered as an offense. When he calls, immediately, you have to open the door of the temple and when he will see you are serving the deities he himself will tell you to continue it. He will not stop you, but your first duty is to go to him immediately when he calls and offer obeisances to him and take permission from him to serve the deities. Mahaprabhu gave us this important teaching through Govinda.

He also gave an important teaching through Jagadanand Pandit. A sanyasi should not use any oil to massage his body and should never sleep on the bed. Jagadanand Pandit was an incarnation of Satyabhama and he has got the ego of her in him. Satyabhama always used to have loving quarrels with Lord Krishna. Incarnation of Satyabhama, Jagadanand Pandit brought a body-cooling-oil having an aromatic fragrance from Gauda-desh for massaging Mahaprabhu's transcendental body. He gave it to Swarup Damodar and asked him to massage Mahaprabhu's head with the oil so that it will cool Him down and He would feel relaxed. Swarup Damodar went to Mahaprabhu with that oil but Mahaprabhu told, “I am a sanyasi and a sanyasi is not supposed to use any oil, especially fragrant oil. Do you want to make Me a darisanyasi (A sanyasi having association with a woman), No, I will not use it.” Then Jaganadand Pandit himself went to Mahaprabhu and told, “I brought this oil from so far with so much effort so please use it.” Mahaprabhu replied, “Then give it in the service of Jagannath”. Mahaprabhu is the Lord Himself but performing the past times of a sanyasi to give us an important teaching. (Guruji suddenly tells about himself) “Oh! I remembered now, I should stop sleeping on the bed. Devotees forced me to sleep on the bed and to sit on chair while having prasādam. Everything is changed now.” Here, Mahaprabhu is giving us an important teaching, being our worshipable Lord, how He spent His life in a small hut, how He ignored His bodily comforts. Even our Prabhupad has also told, “Make your way through this impermanent, transitory life in whatever way you can, keeping the goal of worshiping the Lord foremost in the mind and with the only objective of satisfying the senses of the one, non-dual supreme truth. We would live very comfortably, we would eat nicely, this type of thinking is not good. We should spend our life in the way they have taught us. Saintly persons spend their life in that way only. Do not pay more attention on bodily comforts. Don't abandon the goal of serving the Supreme Lord, even in the face of hundreds of dangers, insults, or persecutions. Never leave Haribhajan or hearing and singing the glories of Krishna, it is everything for us. These are the final instructions of Prabhupad to his disciples. Mahaprabhu also gave these instructions by following them Himself. When Jagadanand Pandit saw Mahaprabhu sleeping on earth, using a saffron colored cloth he made a nice bed and a pillow for Him. Mahaprabhu scolded him saying, “What are you giving Me, do you want to make Me an enjoyer? Then Swarup Damodar made a thin mattress (godadi) from banana tree leaves. Mahaprabhu told, “This is okay.” Mahaprabhu spent eighteen years in Gambhira. Six years He spent in traveling. Another six years, He spent in Puri in which He used to converse with devotees, while the last twelve years He spent completely in solitude, He used to converse only with Swarup Damodar and Ray Ramanand.

Haridas Thakur got a place named 'Balisahi' to stay in which one hut and one 'Tota’, a garden, were there. The place of Mahaprabhu we have seen, is not such a big place then how thousands and thousands persons came there and had darśan of Mahaprabhu? Even two hundred to three hundred persons cannot sit there how can thousands and thousands? It is said that the Lord, in a small child form, stayed on one leaf of a Banyan tree with the full brahmand in Him, then why cannot Kashi Mishra's bhavan accommodate lakhs of persons? Mahaprabhu can do it, we cannot. At that place many devotees came from Gauda-desh and Mahaprabhu is giving them garlands, sandal wood etc. Then He inquired about Haridas Thakur, “Where is Haridas?” One person went outside to see him. He saw Haridas Thakur was offering obeisance to Mahaprabhu from a far distance. He told, “Come, Mahaprabhu is calling you.”

Haridas Thakur replied, “No, I am so lowly a person. I am not allowed to enter into Jagannath temple and Kashi Mishra is a Brahmin, so I should not enter in his house also. That place would become impure. So I should not go there, I offer my pranāms from here.”

When that person informed about this conversation to Mahaprabhu, He went there. When He came to know from Haridas Thakur that he wanted to stay in a secluded place, then he asked Kashi Mishra for such a place in a garden of his house. Kashi Mishra replied, “Everything belongs to You only. Whatever You want to do, You can do.” Then Mahaprabhu went to Haridas Thakur, Haridas immediately fell down in His lotus feet. Mahaprabhu offered him a place near to Him in the garden of Kashi Mishra but out of humbleness Haridas did not accept it. Rupa Goswami and Sanatan Goswami also did not stay there considering themselves the servants of a Muslim King and so impure. Such humbleness, we cannot even imagine! Haridas Thakur is Brahma himself. Then finally Mahaprabhu gave him this place (Siddha Bakul) to stay.

An Arjuna tree stick is given as a tooth brush to Lord Jagannath in the morning. One day, by mistake or by some Divine arrangement one Bakul tree stick got mixed with Arjuna tree sticks and were offered to Lord Jagannath. The offered sticks then used to get distributed to special persons. That day Mahaprabhu got the Bakul tree stick as a prasadam of Jagannath. Mahaprabhu took that stick and came to meet Haridas Thakur at Siddha Bakul. Then He sowed that stick there and immediately it manifested as a big tree. We call it a 'Bakul tree'. Haridas Thakur used to chant three lakhs Holy Names daily beneath this tree and Mahaprabhu Himself used to come here to give him His darśan. After having a bath in the ocean, Mahaprabhu used to go to Haridas Thakur, Rupa and Sanatan Goswami to give them His darśan. So Haridas Thakur performed Bhajan here. As time passed this tree became very big and beautiful. Later when Haridas Thakur disappeared, Jagannath Das who came in his lineage took care of this tree. Once, temple management persons came to cut this tree, they were planning to carve a chariot from it. They thought this is a very big and beautiful tree, only one tree is enough to make the chariots. But the persons taking care of this tree did not allow them to cut it. They told them, “Here Haridas Thakur performed Haribhajan, it is Siddha Bakul, it will not be good to cut it.”

But the persons from temple management did not accept their request. They said, “We are the owner and we will do whatever we want.” So they finally decided a date to cut the Siddha Bakul. When the date came and those persons came and they saw that the whole tree was dried from the inside. They were astonished, “Just a few days ago we saw nice, big tree and now what happened to it?’’ They ran away from there.
Many people tie some clothes and keep them hanging there to fulfill their material desires, which is not good. We should not tie such things to it.
Haridas Thakur performed bhajan here and Mahaprabhu gave him darśan at the time of his disappearance, He danced here and from here He took Haridas Thakur to his samādhi place.

articles.title: Glories of Srila Gadadhara Pandita Goswami
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: In this Harikatha, Srila Gurudev sings the glories of Gadadhara Pandita, who is the fountainhead of all sakti-tattva, non-different from Mahaprabhu and the embodiment of love, Vrndavanesvari Srimati Radhika. He narrates how dear Gadadhara is to Mahaprabhu and how Mahaprabhu is the life and soul of Gadadhara. While narrating his life, Srila Gurudev also emphasizes valuable teachings from his exemplary life.

blocks.text: Like the purpose of Srimad Bhagavatam is to make us listen to the glories of Sri Krishna, His name, form, qualities and pastimes described therein for our eternal welfare, Sri Chaitanya Charitamrta and Sri Chaitanya Bhagavat enable us to know the glories of Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu and His associates. Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu is the cause of that Brahma whom the Gyanis call as 'Advaita Brahma'. The 'Advaita Brahma' is the transcendental halo of the Supreme person, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, or Nandanandana Sri Krishna. The Paramatma form, whom the Yogis meditate upon within their hearts, is also the partial manifestation of the Supreme Lord.
Who is Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu?
He is shada-aishwarya-pati ananta-aishwarya-pati,
“He is the possessor of infinite opulence amongst which these six opulence are main; wealth, potency, strength, fame, beauty, knowledge and renunciation.”

No one else has them to the fullest extent other than the Supreme Lord, Sri Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, who is Sri Krishna Himself. The non-different manifestation of Him is Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. He is not an ordinary devotee. In Gaur-ganodesh-dipika, Kavi Karnapura (son of Shivanandsen) writes about his glories: prema-rupa radha (the manifestation of Radha adorned with the love of Krishna) and vrindavanesvari radha (manifestation of the queen of Vrindavan, Radha). He is the worshiper (Aradhika) of Nandanandan Krishna. He is Gaura-vallabha, the beloved of Gaura. Who is Gaura? He is none other than Nandanandana Krishna who appeared taking the mood and the bodily luster of Srimati Radhika to relish His own sweetness. So Gauranga Mahaprabhu is the combined manifestation of Sri Sri RadhaKrishna. His Antaranga-shakti, internal potency, is Srila Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. Swarupa Damodar, who is Radharani's closest friend and confidante, wrote who Gadadhar Pandit Goswami is; Gadadhar Pandit is Vraja-lakshmi. Lakshmi is the potency of Narayana (Narayan-shakti). The nature of Lakshmi is very peaceful. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami is also peaceful and steady. Lakshmi has different meanings, not only opulence, wealth, etc. Here, Gadadhar Pandit is Prema-lakshmi of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. There are infinite pastimes (Lila) of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu, He performed pastimes as Gaura Narayan as well as Gaura Krishna. Though He is the combined manifestation of Sri RadhaKrishna, He performed different pastimes to impart teachings. During the pastimes of house-hold life He is Gaura-Narayan. In all the pastimes, He has three Shakti (potencies)—Sri, Bhu and Lila. Sri Shakti is Lakshmipriya, Bhu Shakti is Vishnupriya and Lila or Nila is Dhama. In all pastimes, He has these three Shakti. Here (during the Gaur Narayan pastimes), Madhura-rasa is there but not in its complete form. Madhura-rasa is even higher than Vatsalya-rasa. In Madhura-rasa, service is without any hesitation. Madhura-rasa is of two types—Swakiya-rasa (loving relation between Dwarika Queens and Krishna) and the other is Parakiya-rasa (loving relations of Vraja-gopis and Krishna). Pure devotees who wish to attain Vraja-prema, wishing to enter into worship of RadhaGovinda in the top-most Madhura-rasa, have to take shelter of Gadadhar Pandit. Gadadhara-jivan (the life of Gadadhar) and Gadadhara-prandhan (the wealth of Gadadhar) is Gauranga Mahaprabhu.

Where are the deities of Gadai-Gauranga? They are at Champahati, we go there during Nabadwip Dham Parikrama. They were served by Dvija Vaninath. Sri Jayadeva Goswami performed Bhajan there. The king, Lakshman Sen felt sad about Jayadeva Goswami’s leaving Nadadwip Dham and so he offered him to stay at in the village of Champahati where he would not be disturbed by anybody and can perform Bhajan at peace. Champa is a kind of flower which is a golden yellow color. Radharani also has golden complexion. It is the same place where Jayadeva Goswami and Dvija Vaninath had Darshan of Mahaprabhu, first as RadhaKrishna and then in Their combined form as Gauranga Mahaprabhu. We hear Jayadeva Goswami and Dvija Vaninath glories when we go there. If we do not hear, what can we see there with our material eyes? We cannot understand transcendental topics through our material senses. Through transcendental divine eyes only, we can have Darshan of the transcendental divine form of the Lord, the divine form like Krishna holding flute in His hand. Not everybody can have Darshan of Krishna’s beautiful face and experience all types of delightful mellows. If we do not desire to experience that transcendental bliss then what is the use of having this eyes?

Gadadhar Pandit Goswami can award the highest love. We earlier chanted one sloka pañca-tattvātmakaṁ kṛṣṇaṁ bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam bhaktāvatāraṁ bhaktākhyaṁ namāmi bhakta-śaktikam. Ontologically they are one, Gadadhar Pandit Goswami, Radharani are not Shaktiman-tattva (the possessor of the potency), they are Shakti-tattva (potency), complete potency. Shaktiman-tattva is Bhagavan. Bhagavan, ‘Bhaga’ is Vishay-vastu (the object), ‘van’ is one who possesses the potency, He is called Bhagavan. Radharani is Aradhika-shakti (worshiper potency), internal potency (Antaranga-shakti). Likewise, Gadadhar Pandit Goswami is Gauranga’s internal potency, the dear most associate. Those who want to serve the Lord with the mood other than the conjugal love relation (Madhur-rasa), they should take shelter of Nityanand Prabhu. For them Mahaprabhu is Nityananda-jivan (the life of Nityanand). Nityanand Prabhu can give all mellows (Rasa), except the conjugal love (Madhur-rasa). Madhura-rasa is the highest, and pure devotees know that, without the mercy, or without taking shelter of Gadadhar Pandit Goswami they will not get it.

Gadadhar Pandit Goswami appeared in the village named Beleti. Beleti-grama is near Chittagong, which comes in the Dhaka district of Bangladesh. There is a Gadai-Gauranga temple there. Even today, a grand festival is celebrated there on the occasion of the appearance day of Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. There is one Beleti in Assam also. And there also the appearance day of Gadadhar Pandit Goswami is celebrated every year. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami who is Mahaprabhu’s life, (Prana), appeared in 1408 Shakabda (based in Indian National Calendar) accepting Madhava Mishra, who is non-different from Pundarika Vidyanidhi, and Ratnavati Devi as his parents. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami is the complete potency (Purna-shakti) of Mahaprabhu. Therefore, he is present in the pastimes of Mahaprabhu at both places, in Nabadwip as well as in Purushottam Dham. Srivas Pandit is also the potency of the Lord. He is Narad in the pastimes of Krishna. And one who is Radharani in Krishna’s pastimes, Premrupa Radha (the manifestation of Radha adorned with the love of Krishna), Hladini-shakti (the bliss-giving potency), one of Her manifestations is Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. He is a manifestation of Radharani. Another manifestation of Radharani, Chandra-kanti of Radharani—the luster of Radharani, is Gadadhar Das in Gaur-lila. Gadadhar Pandit is Radharani Herself in Krishna-lila, and Gadadhar Das is the luster of Radharani. There are other devotees who are serving the Lord in Dasya, Sakhya, Vatsalya mood. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami, Svarupa Damodar and Raya Ramananda are all under Shakti-tattva, who are Radhika, Lalita and Visakha, respectively. Lalita is the ardent follower of Radharani and one who is following Radha is Anuradha. She also has entered into Gadadhar Pandit Goswami. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami resided at Beleti-gram for twelve years and then came to Nabadwip.

Mukunda Datta, the brother of Vasudev Datta, is from Chattagram. They both are the associates of Mahaprabhu. He got acquainted with Gadadhar Pandit Goswami when the latter came and settled in Nabadwip. Mahaprabhu performed His educational pastimes in Nabadwip. That time, He was known as Nimai Pandit and nobody had the courage to come before Him as He used to debate with everyone and repeatedly refute and re-establish their arguments giving different logic. Hearing His name, everybody used to run away. Srivas Pandit and Mukunda Datta used to converse with each other, but they also were afraid to discuss anything with Nimai Pandit, and seeing Him they also used to run away. One day Mahaprabhu asked Gadadhar Pandit Goswami to give the definition of the word mukti. In response to which Gadadhar Pandit defined mukti as atyantika-duhkha-nivrtti—final and absolute eradication of all miseries. Mahaprabhu refuted it and gave some further explanation and established His statements. All devotees wondered at His brilliant words and understood Him as a great scholar and also wished that He would become a devotee but nobody was able to recognize Him as the Supreme Lord. Mahaprabhu would help Srivas Pandit by carrying his clothes and even sometimes He would wash them. So He was very dedicated to serving Vaishnavas. Srivas Pandit many a time counseled Him saying, “These arguments and logic are meant for scholars. People study in order to become devotees of Krishna. What is the use of this scholarship if one does not surrender unto the Lotus Feet of Krishna and become His devotee?” Then Mahaprabhu would say, “By your blessings I will surely become a devotee one day.” The Lord Himself is speaking, but Srivas Pandit is not recognizing Him so, how will others understand? He is meeting Him in person, getting attracted to Him, conversing with Him, but not realizing that He is Supreme Lord!

The Lord is showing humbleness, “By your blessing I will become a devotee soon.” Later after returning from Gaya, He began to reveal ecstatic symptoms of Divine Love. Srivas Pandit was the first to notice that and reported it to all other devotees who were overjoyed to receive that news. Then Mahaprabhu decided to fulfill the wish of the devotees and revealed His true identity to them and manifested His Mahaprakash-lila.

He declared, “I will meet all devotees at Shuklambar Brahmachari’s house to fulfill their wishes.” Gadadhar Pandit went there in advance and hid himself in the house of Shuklambar Brahmachari. But on seeing Mahaprabhu’s ecstasies of love, he fainted. Later, Gadadhar Pandit Goswami used to stay close to Mahaprabhu, always. Once when Mahaprabhu intensely yearned for the Darshan of Krishna, and cried in separation, calling, “Where is My Prananath (the master of My life)?” That time Gadadhar Pandit told, “Krishna is within Your heart only.” Listening to this, Mahaprabhu desperately started to claw at His chest. Sachi Mata was there nearby, witnessing all this. Out of her great affection for her Son, she feared, “He will hurt Himself.” She is Yashodadevi in Krishna-lila. That time, Gadadhar Pandit, who is very dear to Gaurang Mahaprabhu, pacified Him. Witnessing this Sachi Mata said, “Gadadhar, you always stay near Nimai.” And from that time onwards Gadadhar Pandit stayed near to Him always.

We are attached to the material world, how can we understand this loving attachment of the transcendental world? How can we understand the loving attachment of Gadadhar Pandit Goswami to Mahaprabhu? Gadadhar Pandit Goswami observed strict Brahmacarya from his childhood. Seeing his firm determination, Ishvara Puripad made him read his own book, Krishna-lilamrit.

Pundarika Vidyanidhi, an associate of Mahaprabhu, was also from Chattagram, who later came to Nabadwip Dham and stayed there. No one recognized him as he disguised himself as a great sense enjoyer in order to mask his devotional feelings. Once Mukund told Gadadhar Pandit that there is one Vaishnava he knows and he wants to introduce Gadadhar to him. Saying so, he took him to Pundarika Vidyanidhi’s house. When Pundarika Vidyanidhi arrived at Nabadwip, Mahaprabhu uttered ‘Pundarika re, baap re amar—O Pundarika, my father!’ Srimati Radharani’s father, Vrishabhanu has come as Pundarika Vidyanidhi in Gaura-lila. So in that relation Mahaprabhu addressed him as, “O My father, Pundarika!” When Mukund arrived at Pundarika’s house with Gadadhar Pandit, Gadadhar Pandit saw that Pundarika was surrounded by expensive furnishings, milky white foam bedding, and many other objects of enjoyment. Gadadhar, not understanding Pundarika’s inner mood, thought, “What kind of Vaishnava is he? And where has Mukund brought me? He seems like a sense enjoyer!” Pundarika is King Vrishabhanu in Krishna-lila, Gadadhar’s own father but he could not recognize him. His identity was covered and his inner mood also was hidden by external objects of sense enjoyment.
Mukund sensed Gadadhar Pandit’s mind and immediately recited one shloka from Srimad Bhagavatam, to reveal Pundarika Vidyanidhi’s inner mood,

“Sister of Bakasura, Baki, Putana, went to kill Krishna by smearing her breasts with Kalakuta poison. She spoke sweetly and took Child Krishna on her lap, and Krishna was pleased by her motherly affection even in her pretense, Krishna awarded her the position of a wet nurse, a motherly place. Whose shelter shall I take other than Him?”

As soon as Pundarika heard him, he began to cry, uttering ‘Ha Krishna!’ and fell on the ground and fainted. Everything around him including his clothes got scattered here and there. Out of feelings of ecstasy his body started showing symptoms of transformation. Gadahar Pandit was amazed to see this reaction and realized that he has committed an offense to him considering him to be an ordinary man. He understood that his separation grief from Krishna is so much that even a little remembrance of Him maddens him. No ordinary person can have such feelings. In reality, Pundarika is father of Gadadhar Pandit. Gadadhar asked Mahaprabhu what needs to be done to become relieved from the offense he has commited thinking Pundarika to be an ordinary man. Mahaprabhu advised him to take initiation, Diksha, from him to get free from the offense. And thus Gadadhar took initiation from Pundarika Vidyanidhi and became his disciple.

Pundarika Vidyanidhi did not go to Ganges during the day time as it was difficult for him to see people use the holy waters of Ganges for their day-to-day activities, like cleaning teeth, washing clothes, etc. So he would go for her Darshan at midnight and would offer obeisance to her from a distance. He has the feeling that how can he touch his feet to the holy waters of Ganges? So he never took bath in the Ganges. Likewise, our Param Gurudev, Srila Bhakti Siddhant Sarasvati Thakur Prabhupad also, showed the same ideal and never took bath in Radhakunda which is non-different from Srimati Radhika. He offered Pranam to Radhakunda water and took it on his head. We should not imitate him; we are not on that platform.

Gadadhar Pandit Goswami participated in Mahaprabhu’s pastimes at Srivas Angan, in the pastimes of deliverance of Chandkazi, in Gundicha Marjan pastimes, in Jagannath Rathayatra pastimes etc. When Sachi Mata ordered Mahaprabhu to be in Nilachal (Jagannath Puri) after His renounced order of life (Sanyas), Gadadhar Pandit also took the vow of Shketra-sanyas at Nilachal (the vow of not going out of Nilachal for his full life) so that Mahaprabhu would not tell him to go away from Him. He was ordered by Sachi Mata to be with Mahaprabhu always, and personally also he wanted to be with Him always. When Tota Gopinath deity manifested at Nilachal Dham, Mahaprabhu gave His service responsibilities to Gadadhar Pandit. Tota Gopinathji’s form is beautiful and He has a tall figure. Gadadhar Pandit Goswami was engaged in His service, blissfully. When he grew old and was unable to serve the deity in His standing position, Gopinath mercifully sat down to accept the loving service of Gadadhar Pandit! Once Nityananda Prabhu came there and brought very fine rice as an offering for Gopinath. Gadadhar Pandit cooked the rice along with some vegetables he himself grew in the garden nearby. When he was offering Bhoga to the deity, Mahaprabhu also appeared there and gave him great pleasure. Later the three of them joyfully took Prasad together.

During the Chaturmasa-vrata (the four months vow during the monsoon season) all the devotees from Nabadwipa (from Gauda-desh) used to come to Mahaprabhu at Nilachal and used to stay with Him until Rathayatra. Mahaprabhu had the desire to go to Vrindavan for a long time. After the third year’s stay of Gaudiya devotees in Nilachal Dham, when they left after Rathayatra, Mahaprabhu decided to go to Vrindavan. King Prataparudra was a great devotee of the Lord and he knew all the places of his kingdom where Mahaprabhu was going to pass during His journey to Vrindavan. The Lord gave him the service opportunity to make arrangements at different places. Mahaprabhu started His journey to Vrindavan and that time Ramananda Raya and other devotees also joined Him. Gadadhar Pandit also joined Mahaprabhu for Vrindavan. Mahaprabhu became worried about Gadadhar and after a while asked him to go back to Nilachal so not to break his vow of Kshetra-sanyas. In reply to that, Gadadhar told Him that wherever He is, that place is Nilachal Dham. He also mentioned that let this vow of Kshetra-sanyas go to Rasatal (the bottom planet), he is not worried about it at all. Such a strong loving attachment Gadadhar has towards Mahaprabhu. He is not able to bear His separation even for a moment. Those who have entered into the realm of spontaneous loving devotion (Prema-bhakti) only, can comprehend his feelings, not those who follow the devotion with rules and regulations (Vidhi-bhakti).
Mahaprabhu again said, “Giving up vows would amount to offense; you are abandoning the service of Gopinath.”
Gadadhar replied, “By serving You, crores of Gopinath will be served. I will take all the responsibilities for any offense to Gopinath.”

Can anybody understand his love? Gadadhar said, “I will not go with you. I am going to see Sachi Mata.” Saying so, he started walking alone. When they arrived at Cuttack, Mahaprabhu again called Gadadhar and asked him, “Do you want to fulfill My desire or your own desire? Do you want My happiness or your happiness? If you wish to make Me happy then you should not leave Purushottam Dhama.” Hearing so Gadadhar fainted and fell down. We will not understand what this love is! Such a deep attachment!

Mahaprabhu exhibited His earthly pastimes for forty-eight years. And after Mahaprabhu’s departure Gadadhar Pandit remained on this earth only for eleven months, always absorbed in the separation grief of Mahaprabhu. Mahaprabhu appeared to distribute this highest Divine Love to all the conditioned souls of this world. To attain this love we have to surrender to Gadadhar Pandit and pray for his mercy. We have to also pray to our Guruvarga for their mercy. Then we can attain this supreme bliss, Unnata-ujjvala-rasa. Even Krishna is desirous of relishing that love. Krishna says,

In aisvarya-bhava, in love with reverence, love becomes sankucita, constricted. Therefore, in mora putra, mora sakhā, mora prāṇa-pati such bhava (considering Him to be their own son, bosom friend, the owner of one’s life), there is no hesitation in the service of Nandanandana Krishna.

Vallabha Bhatta came to Mahaprabhu and desired to listen to scriptural conclusions from Him. As he had false pride in him, Mahaprabhu showed indifference towards him. So he went to Gadadhar Pandit who is very soft natured, the same as Rukmini has in Krishna’s pastimes. When Krishna showed indifference to Rukmini, she thought Krishna would leave her and thinking so, she used to become afraid and used to cry. So Gadadhar Pandit also became afraid that Mahaprabhu would leave his association when He exhibiting some sort of coldness towards him because of his association with Vallabh Bhatta. He immediately went to Mahaprabhu and, holding His feet, he cried. So Mahaprabhu is called Gadadhar-prana, Gadadhar’s life and soul. Now sing kirtan of Gadai-Gauranga.

articles.title: Harikatha on the Day of Gundicha Marjan
articles.author: Sreela Bhakti Ballabh Tirtha Goswami Maharaj
articles.excerpt: In this harikatha, Srila Gurudev narrates about Gundicha-marjan-lila. He starts with explaining the meaning of Gundicha and how Gundicha-marjan was started by Mahaprabhu. He explains Mahaprabhu’s mood while having the darshan of Jagannath Dev and also narrates the pastime of Lord Krishna’s meeting the Vraja-vasi at Kurukshetra. The Vraja-vasi wants Krishna to go to Vrindavan along with them and they request this of Him. Sriman Mahaprabhu, in the mood of Radharani, pulls Jagannath’s chariot taking Him from Kurukshetra to Vrindavan.

blocks.text: What is the meaning of Gundicha-marjan? Gundicha was the wife of King Indradyumna Maharaj. Indradyumna Maharaj was ordered by Jagannath Deva, “Take Me, Baladeva and Subhadra in chariots to Gundicha, your wife’s place. It is My place of appearance.” Near Gundicha is situated ‘Bankamuhana’ (Chakra Tirtha) where Lord Jagannath Deva appeared as dāru-brahma—in the form of transcendental wood. It is written in Ṛg Veda—dāruplavatesindhoh pāre apurusam. Ṛg Veda tells the truth. It is not false. He (dāru-brahma) is beyond nature. He is not the creation of any person of this material world. He told Indradyumna Maharaj, “You do not worry. What if you have not got the darśan of My Nilamadhava form?”
“Where?”
“At Bankemuhana, which is two miles from the main Jagannath temple. From Jagannath temple I will go to the appearance place where you performed a thousand Ashwamedha Yagyas.”

When Mahaprabhu went to Purushottam Dham, He first arrived at ‘Atharah-nāla’. Srila Gurumaharaj established the lotus feet of Sriman Mahaprabhu at that place which is being worshiped by the devotees. When Mahaprabhu arrived at ‘Atharah-nāla’, He saw the Jagannath temple from there and on the top of it He saw Krishna in the form of a small child playing a flute in His hand.

Mahaprabhu was coming to Purusottam Dham with Nityanand Prabhu and other devotees and He had His sannyās-daṇḍa with Him which He accepted from a gyāna-margiya-sampradāya—who does not consider the personal form of the Supreme Lord. Mahaprabhu is the Supreme Lord, why would He carry a sannyās-daṇḍa with Him? We conditioned souls have to accept daṇḍa—sharir-daṇḍa, man-daṇḍa, vāka-daṇḍa (punishment for the sins incurred by body mind and speech). So when Mahaprabhu was in the mood of ecstasy, Nityananda Prabhu broke His daṇḍa into three pieces and threw it in a river. Mahaprabhu enquired, “Where is My daṇḍa?” Nityanand Prabhu replied, “When You were fully intoxicated with love, You fell on it and it broke, so we threw it away.”
Mahaprabhu: “Because of My accompanying you all, My only support, My daṇḍa is destroyed. You have taken My wealth. I will not go with you all. First you all go, and then I will come.”
Nityananda Prabhu: “No, No. You are always in ecstatic mood, how will we look after You if You come later? So You go first and we will follow You.”

Therefore, He went first. After reaching Jagannath temple, seeing Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra, He became unconscious. (Srila Gurudev says about himself out of humbleness:) I went there so many times but nothing had happened to me. So many people go there. There is lot of difference in darśan. We see, “What is this, incomplete hands, legs etc?” Lord Himself came as Ananta Maharāṇā to carve deities from the dāru and showed the pastime of not completing Them fully. Ananta Maharāṇā asked King Indradyumna to open the doors of the room (where he was carving the deities) after twenty one days. But when there was no sound coming from the room, the King and the Queen became worried and they opened the door after fifteen days. Seeing the incomplete forms of the Lord, Indradyumna Maharaj fell unconscious. The Lord said ‘’I desired to stay in this form only.’’ How did the forms of Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra become manifest who we see now?

Baladeva, Subhadra and Jagannath were in Dwarka. Krishna enacted the pastime of staying in Dwarka and not in Vrindavan. At first, from Vrindavan He came to Mathura after which He did not go back to Vrindavan. Actually, He is in Vrindavan only. To increase the separation mood of Vraja-vasis, He enacted the pastimes of not staying in Vrindavan, externally. In prema, union and separation both are necessary. In separation of Krishna the Vraja-vasis used to cry incessantly. Nanda Maharaj and Yashoda Devi became so weak from separation. Yashoda Devi cries in separation all the time, “For whom do I cook for? Gopal nai—Gopal is not here.” Nanda Baba also cries all the time. All the friends are crying, “We have become poor. Gopal has now become a King in Dwarka and has forgotten us.”

One day Rohini Devi came to Dwarka. While having a conversation with the Dwarka queens, she said, “You all are so fortunate that Krishna, attracted by your love, stays with you. He doesn’t go to Vraja. Vraja-vasis are always crying, what is their fault?”

Then, the queens said, “This is untrue, Krishna stays with us from the outside, not from the heart. In the night, it is not our names He takes and cries. At all time, He calls out the names of Gopis and Sakhas. His body is here but actually He is there. He doesn't love us. Why does He not take our names? We all sleep at one place but He never took our names. What is the reason?”
Rohini Devi said, “I can tell you about Vrindavan but Krishna and Balaram should not come here.”
The queens told, “Subhadra will become the guard. She will not allow Them to come. Do not worry.”
When Rohini Devi started speaking about the Divine Love of Gopis for Krishna everyone listened attentively.

Krishna says to Narad, mad-bhaktā yatra gāyanti tatra tiṣṭhāmi nārada—wherever My devotees sings My glories I stay there. So Krishna and Balaram also came there. Krishna and Balaram started listening to Rohini Devi. By listening to the ecstatic Vraja pastimes, Divine Love manifested and Their hands and legs shortened and Their eyes became big. This manifestation happened in Subhadra also. That same form is seen in Puri. People like us do not have such darśan. Mahaprabhu was seeing Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra as the manifestation of highest Divine Love of the Gopis. Mahaprabhu is enacting the pastime of a devotee, taking the mood of Radharani. Without taking the mood of a devotee Himself, He cannot teach everyone. Therefore, He adorned the mood of a devotee and showed them how to render service unto the Supreme Lord. Everyone learns by seeing His conduct. He knows everything. He is always absorbed in the mood of Radharani. He does not see the Lord the way we all see Him. He sees Lord Jagannath Deva as His loving Lord Krishna whom Radharani is attached to. Therefore, He fell unconscious. What do we see when we go? No hands, no feet. I am not a person of that level. I am a conditioned soul—anartha yukt baddha jīva. Having bodily conception, me and mine mentality. I have material eyes. What will we understand? We listen to these topics but we do not have any understanding. Jagadish Pandit, who is a personal associate of the Lord, by crying in separation brought Jagannath Deva to Chakadah from Nilachal Dham. We cannot bring Him. He will not listen to us. We do not have love for Him. We just do an external showoff.

Chaitanya Mahaprabhu initiated Gundicha Marjan. King Prataparudra, Kashi Mishra and Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, all followed the orders of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu. If Chaitanya Mahaprabhu says something, nobody can go against it. He said, “A day prior to Lord Jagannath Deva’s going to Gundicha, I asked for a service to be performed there. We will all go there and clean the temple.”
Until the time we have other desires in our hearts, we cannot have real darśan of Jagannath, Baladeva and Subhadra. And therefore, until then real Rathayatra also does not happen.
Mahaprabhu said, “I request for an order from Kashi Mishra (of Radhakant Math) and principle person Vasudeva Sarvabhauma for granting us the service”.
Kashi Mishra, responded, “Oh, You are requesting for service! The service of cleaning of the temple is not suitable for You but by this You want to enact some pastime so let it happen.”
He immediately made all the arrangements. Mahaprabhu took everyone to Gundicha. What is the mood of Mahaprabhu while taking Jagannath to Gundicha?
“I have finally found the Lord of My life, for whom I had so long burned in the flames of desire.”
The chariot represents the opulence (aiśvarya-bhāva), elephants, horses, etc. From there the Lord is taken to Gundicha, Vrindavan.

As on the occasion of a solar eclipse, it is one of the duties of the king to please the citizens. So all the citizens of Dwarka got ready to go to Kurukshetra for the solar eclipse. The King also had to go. An invitation was sent to everyone for the festivity. But Vraja-vasis were not invited. Narad Rishi thought that Vraja-vasis are so sweet. They quit eating and everything (because of their separation from Krishna), but they are not invited. His heart was broken.
He complained to Krishna, “You invited the whole world but You did not invite Vraja-vasis. Why so? I am not able to bear this”.

Krishna said, “Vraja-vasis are My own. Do parents invite their son? Does the son invite the parents? Relatives are invited. Parents are not invited as they are our own. And one more reason is that Brahmins will perform karma-kāṇḍīya sacrifices there, if they do come, all the karma-kāṇḍīya sacrifices will get destroyed and their desires will not be fulfilled.”

Then Narad Rishi became quiet. Kurukshetra is situated near Vrindavan. When Krishna’s friends, Gopis and other Vraja-vasis came to know that Krishna has come to Kurukshetra, all of them gathered at a place and thought, “We are cowherd boys and girls. Krishna is a great King. He has so much grandeur, why would He meet us? He can forget everything but He cannot forget His father and mother. Therefore, we should take Nanda Maharaj and Yashoda Mata along with us. When He will come to see them, we will get a chance to meet Him.”

They went to Nanda Maharaj and Yashoda Mata and said, “We are poor cowherd people, we may not be able to see Krishna but if you go there He will definitely come to pay obeisances. He has forgotten us, we are poor, if we go He will not meet us.”
They requested them again and again. Then, Nanda Maharaj and Yashoda Mata agreed and said, “We will go but if we do not get His darśan then we will leave our body there only. This is our condition.”
“No, don’t worry, you will get darśan.”

There in Kurukshetra, the King, Krishna, had brought a great chariot, a huge army and constructed a great building. Nobody was allowed to meet Krishna. Brahmins are performing sacrifices and Krishna is sitting there. Vraja-vasis reached the gate.
The gatekeepers asked them, ‘’Who are you?”
They said, “Our son is inside.”
“Who is your son?”
“Krishna.”
“No. His parents are Vasudeva and Devaki. They are there inside. Where have you come from? You are poor. Whose parents are you? We cannot allow you to enter. These are the rules here.”
They started crying.
“What is the use of crying? You say He is your son. But His parents are inside. Where have you come from? Present some proof.”
There were four gates. They went to all the gates. They asked but they were not allowed in. Then they requested to open the gate a little bit so that they can see Him from a distance.
“No, we will get fired. There are Brahmins performing sacrifices. We cannot allow you.”
Then they thought, “We have already said that we are poor, He has forgotten us, He is a King now with so much opulence. There is no hope to meet Him. We will leave this body.”

“Gopal... Gopal...” they called out loudly and cried. The King was sitting in the arena of sacrifice. He stood up immediately, removed and threw off all His clothes and ran naked calling, “Maa...Maa…” He came running and embraced mother Yashoda. He was also in pain from inside. Mother Yashoda had tears in her eyes…calling, “Gopal…Gopal…” Nand Maharaj also uttered, “Gopal…Gopal…” All the sakhās uttered. “bhāi Kanaiya….” (dear brother Kanaiya). Due to their arrival, all the karma-kāṇḍīya activates got destroyed. Brahmins became surprised at what had happened.
Krishna said, “It is not possible to stay here now as they are here, so bring the chariots.”
He said to the Vraja-vasis, “We have some pending work, we will come soon after finishing that.”
All the Gopis said, “Hey Gopinath, Hey Gopinath.. Vrindavane chalo Hey Gopinath”—Hey Gopinath, Hey Gopinath, let us go to Vrindavan, Hey Gopinath.

With this mood, Mahaprabhu was pulling the chariots. Where would He take them from Kuruskhetra? To Vrindavan..Gundicha…Gundicha means Vrindavan Dham. Krishna is in a different mood there. Mahaprabhu is walking with tears in His eyes.

Gopis says, “Here, we see lokāraṇya—horses and elephants etc. and the royal persons. We are not feeling happy here. Meeting You is nice but please come to Vrindavan. There is no opulence in Vrindavan but there is sweet affection there.”
Then Lord said,
“Devotional service unto Me is the cause of attaining Me. It is My great fortune that you all love Me. I can be attained only by love, nothing else. I am coming, do not worry.”
Mahaprabhu accepted that mood. Rupa Goswami says,

lines: (Bhakti-rasamrita-sindhu 1.1.11 quoted in Sri Chaitanya Charitamrita Madhya 19.167)

blocks.text:
To get this Divine Love one has to become devoid of desires other than the service of Krishna, you have to leave the processes of gyāna and karma and have to serve Krishna in the association of devotees.
All sorts of desires should be cleared off as sand, stones, small rocks are cleared. All this should be thrown far away. There should not be any desire left in the heart. The efforts for karma and gyāna should also be left. Srila Narottam Das Thakur writes,

lines: nānā yoni sadā phire, kadarya bhakṣaṇa kare

blocks.text: “The fruitive worker of karma-kāṇḍa and the speculations of gyāna-kāṇḍa are two pots of poison. If one drinks these two poisons, and then proclaims that they are both as sweet as nectar, he will fall from the human realm and spend a long time wandering in many species of life, eating many abominable things, and enjoying many horrible pleasures.”

One cannot achieve the Lord by karma-kāṇḍa and gyāna-kāṇḍa. All desires must be removed. Therefore, Mahaprabhu gave them the broom for cleaning. The debris and dirt collected by everyone together was not even equal to that collected by Mahaprabhu alone. He inspired everyone, and told them that all sorts of egos will have to be removed and then devotion will have to be performed. The method to remove desires from the heart is to perform Harinam. They brought a hundred pots filled with water. With every sweep and every pot of water used for cleaning, ‘Hare Krishna’ was being chanted.
Mahaprabhu is instructing, “Do Harinam”,
He says, nāma-saṅkīrtana — kalau param aupāya.
Everything is inside the Name. It is said,

lines: harer nāma harer nāma harer nāmaiva kevalam
kalau nāsty eva nāsty eva nāsty eva gatir anyathā.

blocks.text: They keep on chanting Harinam. Krishna’s Name, form, qualities, pastimes, everything is inside the Name. But chanting should be done with the mood that, “I am of Him”.
